extracted.intended_audience: readers, literary translators, editors, and distributors/republishers of Project Gutenberg eBooks
extracted.subtask_short: translating Don Quixote and redistributing PG
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing (translating and editing) an English edition of Don Quixote together with the Project Gutenberg redistribution/legal requirements. Covers translatorly principles (fidelity, tone, diction, names) and Project Gutenberg license/redistribution rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affectation in translation
rubrics_metrics.description: One rigid rule in translating Don Quixote is to avoid everything that savours of affectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book itself is a protest against affectation; a translator should resist the temptation to use antiquated or obsolete language which would be an affectation without warrant. The translator's aim should be simplicity and plain everyday language except where the original calls for otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simple, plain, everyday language
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in the tales and Don Quixote’s speeches, the translator who uses the simplest and plainest everyday language will almost always be the one who approaches nearest to the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spanish has probably undergone less change since the seventeenth century than other European languages, and much of Don Quixote differs little from colloquial Spanish of later times—so modern, simple English better preserves the original's flavour than artificially archaic diction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve names and familiar phrases unless reasoned
rubrics_metrics.description: The old familiar names and phrases should not be changed without good reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since the story and its characters are household words in English, retain familiar anglicized names/phrases unless there is a compelling reason to alter them; translators should be cautious about unnecessary changes that disrupt readers' expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity to matter, letter, and spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Translator’s first duty is to those who look for as faithful a representation of the author as possible: 'faithful to the letter so long as fidelity is practicable, faithful to the spirit so far as he can make it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to represent both the content (matter) and method (the way Cervantes tells the story). Pleasing a casual reader is desirable but should not trump conscientious fidelity; where possible, preserve the author's idiom, sententious terseness, and comic method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect Quixotic humour's unsmiling gravity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that the humour of Don Quixote often depends on sententious terseness and an unsmiling gravity; translators should avoid turning it into mere buffoonery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jocular embellishment or flippancy (e.g., 'cockney flippancy') that falsifies the spirit of the book. Maintain the balance between humour and seriousness that Cervantes uses—do not 'bring Cervantes forward smirking and grinning at his own good things.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid needless archaisms and literal mistranslations
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid antiquated language and barbarously literal translations; literalness can be as damaging as excessive looseness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The translator should not adopt archaic formulations merely to look 'old'; literal, unadapted renderings of words may be inappropriate in many contexts. Strive for natural, idiomatic English that conveys sense and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscientiousness over fashionable liberties
rubrics_metrics.description: There are readers who want the story as Cervantes tells it; give preference to a conscientious translator even if awkward at times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not sacrifice authorial method for contemporary amusement. If possible, aim to please both casual and exacting readers, but prioritize faithful representation of author's technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate/credit editorial/illustrative additions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial choices such as attaching illustrations not part of the original should be noted explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Project Gutenberg edition notes that Doré engravings were not part of the original Ormsby translation and explains the editorial decision. When adding materials (plates, covers, images), document their provenance and relation to the source text.
